items.title: How Do Banking Supervisors Deal with Failing Banks?
authors: Sergio Correia, Stephan Luck, and Emil Verner
items.excerpt: In this post, we discuss insights from a recent staff report on the role of banking supervision in identifying and disciplining failing banks. We show that bank failures typically result from supervisory closure decisions based on hard information about book equity. Yet hard information is itself partly produced by supervision, as our evidence suggests that supervisors require troubled banks to recognize potential losses. …

explained.headline: Thousands of opposition supporters rally in Delhi to demand election chief's resignation

happened.text: Tens of thousands of opposition supporters gathered at Ramlila Maidan in central Delhi to demand the resignation of India's chief election commissioner, Gyanesh Kumar.
Organised by the opposition INDIA bloc and led by Rahul Gandhi's Congress party, the protest featured prominent regional leaders and speeches criticising the government.
Rahul Gandhi said the opposition would take legal action regarding vote theft and warned Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Home Minister Amit Shah.

background.text: The protest follows weeks of demonstrations over the Special Intensive Revision, a controversial process that removed more than 130 million names from India's draft electoral rolls.
Opposition parties allege that the voter list revision disproportionately targeted Muslims and other minorities to benefit Prime Minister Narendra Modi's ruling Bharatiya Janata Party.

matters.text: Human Rights Watch said the accusations regarding the voter roll revision raise serious questions about the fairness of future Indian elections.
Bharatiya Janata Party leader and federal minister JP Nadda said the opposition rally was a calculated conspiracy to plunge the nation into anarchy under the guise of defending democracy.

uncertain.text: It remains unclear whether the opposition can overcome a significant trust deficit and successfully unite disparate youth movements, such as the Cockroach Janta Party, with established political parties.
Questions persist regarding the true level of widespread public mobilisation and whether the opposition can build a viable electoral challenge against the ruling party.

terms.definition: The head of the body responsible for administering election processes in the country.

removed.text: The Election Commission maintains that the revision aims to remove duplicate registrations and ineligible individuals, while the Bharatiya Janata Party and election officials have denied all allegations of bias.
why: Evidence does not support the claim that all allegations were denied, just the commission's position.

removed.text: The opposition alliance views the campaign against the chief election commissioner as an essential first step to protect democratic processes in the country.
why: The claim states the view as fact; it should be attributed to Rahul Gandhi or the opposition.

also.title: Germany news: Gen Z group calls for new protests

happened.text: Shops were looted and emergency services were targeted with fireworks, stones and bottles during clashes in Frankfurt, Cologne and Hamburg after weekend protests.
Authorities in Frankfurt reported that stones and petrol bombs were thrown, shop windows were smashed, and more than 100 police officers were injured.
Police in Berlin reported that 27 officers were injured and up to 56 people were temporarily detained following a smaller demonstration.

background.text: Tens of thousands of young people joined largely peaceful demonstrations organised by the campaign group Gen Z regelt to protest against underfunding in schools, living costs, spending cuts and military service.
Federal Interior Minister Alexander Dobrindt stated that peaceful demonstrations had been hijacked towards the evening by violence-prone left-wing groups and migrant anarchists.
Education Minister Karin Prien argued that the violence indicated that the integration of people of migrant background into German society could be improved.

matters.text: Chancellor Friedrich Merz stated that the government would show no tolerance for violence, emphasising that offenders would feel the full force of the law.
Chancellor Friedrich Merz also highlighted a positive aspect to the protests, stating that the young generation is politically engaged and concerned about its future.

uncertain.text: Defence Minister Boris Pistorius questioned the generalisations made about migrant groups, asking where to stop differentiating and stating that he could not quickly verify the facts.
Officials and researchers debated the precise identities and backgrounds of the individuals who carried out the acts of violence during the unrest.

terms.definition: A major centre-right political party in Germany.

removed.text: Climate activist Luisa Neubauer criticised the focus on violence, arguing that the debate was treated as a found pleasure by people not seriously interested in youth concerns.
